title: Second largest value
objective: second_largest(numbers) should return the second largest distinct value in the list.
expected: Repeated values only count once. If there is no second distinct value, return None.
constraints: Do not modify the list that is passed in.

advice.diagnosis: ordered[-2] on line 4 crashes when the list has fewer than two items, because there is no second element to read.
advice.rationale: Adding a length check before sorting returns None for short lists and keeps the existing logic for everything else.
advice.note: Partially correct. The length check fixes the crash, but duplicates are never removed, so [5, 5, 3] returns 5 and [4, 4] returns 4.

staticWarnings.message: Possible logic issue: ordered[-2] depends on duplicate values. The docstring asks for a distinct value, but duplicates are not removed before indexing.

prediction.question: After applying the suggested patch, what does second_largest([5, 5, 3]) return?

suspiciousLineCheck.question: The code checker flagged line 6 of the patch. What could go wrong there?
options: If the largest value appears twice, ordered[-2] is that same largest value
Negative indexes cannot be used on a sorted list
sorted() changes the list that was passed in
Nothing, the length check on line 3 already covers every case
suspiciousLineCheck.answer: If the largest value appears twice, ordered[-2] is that same largest value
